key_insight: WebSwarm turns web search into a recursive delegation process, letting agents expand, solve, and aggregate evidence hierarchically to better handle both depth and coverage.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical orchestration pattern for building more capable research agents that need scalable web exploration, evidence grounding, and adaptive collaboration.
method: Probes how task-relevant information is organized on the web before expanding nodes.
Instantiates agentic search nodes with local objectives and search modes.
Allows nodes to solve locally or delegate child nodes, then pass evidence/results upward for revision and aggregation.
evidence_signal: The paper reports consistent gains over single-agent and multi-agent baselines on BrowseComp-Plus, WideSearch, DeepWideSearch, and GISA, covering deep, wide, and interleaved search tasks.
watch_item: Recursive delegation and node expansion can increase orchestration complexity and tool usage, so efficiency and stopping criteria need careful control.
paper_title: WebSwarm: Recursive Multi-Agent Orchestration for Deep-and-Wide Web Search
